title: Model 2 surface current product comparison on Caribbean drifters
scope: Replacing the model surface current with an observation-based current product in a drift recipe, scored on 48 independent undrogued drifters in the eastern Caribbean (2,423 cases, June 2022 to August 2024); fitted arms scored on held-out drifters by 5-fold split.
summary: The observation-based current product cut trajectory miss by roughly 30 to 40% at 24, 48 and 72 h. At 48 h the median miss was 20.2 km for the product alone against 29.9 km for the model current plus 2% wind, and the mean difference was -9.7 km (interval -11.6 to -7.4). A forecast-capable form (slow part frozen before issue, wind-driven part rebuilt) kept most of the gain (48 h mean -8.4 km, interval -10.4 to -6.0, with analysis wind standing in for forecast wind). On the four Puerto Rico GPS mats the same recipe tied the existing recipe and was worse in the tail.

limitations: The source report is an untracked working-tree file; it is identified by SHA-256 only and has no source commit.
Drifters are not Sargassum; on the Puerto Rico GPS mats the recipe tied (medians 12.07/22.52 vs 11.73/22.38 km at 24/48 h) and had a worse 90th percentile.
Forecast mode uses analysis wind in place of forecast wind, which is optimistic.
Fitted arms used a 5-fold split by drifter, but the product comparison is exposed development evidence.

Adding 2% wind to a surface model current made drifters worse, consistent with double counting wind-driven flow; the finding that the model current is overweighted reproduces the half-weight result from GPS tracks.
